evidence.requirements: Almost all of the brief is implemented. The start page has the heading, the Search and Family controls, the 'n cartridges' count and exact-name links (list.jpg; app.js:37-71). Search ignores spaces and case, so '7,62 x 51' finds 308 Win. (core.js:104-114). The detail view lists every fact the brief asks for, including capacity with a source link, and shows all cartridge and chamber sections in Symbol/Value/Unit tables with tolerances merged into the value (detail-308_win.jpg; core.js:130-144). Print button, 'All cartridges' link and hash routes that survive a reload are present (app.js:151-196). Partly met: (1) the shoulder angle α gets only a leader and a label (core.js:675-685, 735-740). The brief asks for a dimension with arrowheads and extension lines. (2) The title block gives the scale as 'True to scale (1 mm = 1 unit); fitted to width' (app.js:123), not as an actual scale. (3) 'Labels do not overlap': extension lines run through labels such as R and R1. On 9,3 x 74 R the L2 and L6 dimension lines share one line. (4) On straight cases the inner wall tapers from tb to tn over the whole body (core.js:395-397). The brief says tb along the body. Not visible in the delivery: no spec, plan or review artefacts from the required process.
evidence.correctness: The geometry follows the rules closely. Rim type uses the R1/P1 thresholds (core.js:72-88). The chamfer is min(f·tanβ, R1/4) (core.js:310-313). The rimfire half-round has radius min(R/2,(R1-P1)/2) (core.js:297-307). The groove runs floor, then a ramp to (P1/2, E). The belt ramps at δ out to R3/2, follows it to E, then steps in (core.js:320-337). The shoulder passes through the published points with r1 min and r2 fillets (core.js:365-372). Bullet seating s and cylinder fraction k come from the shape and category tables. The nose is a tangent ogive with the brief's ρ, a quarter ellipse, or a cone (core.js:431-469). The heeled case uses H2 outside and H2-2tb for the heel (core.js:426-470). The section walls use the brief's tn, tb and w, and the primer-pocket table is correct (core.js:90-101, 378-386). Proportions match the reference drawings: 308_win, 9_mm_luger and 22_long_rifle line up with reference/*.png. Dimension values and tolerances are correct ('L1 39.62 -0.2', 'R 1.4 -0.25'). Angles show as 40° and 10°58'00". The print of 308 Win. fits one A4 page (print-308_win.jpg). Defects: in detail-9_3_x_74_r.jpg the L2 and L6 dimension lines are collinear in one lane. segmentsCross ignores collinear overlap (core.js:537-543), so L2's arrow lands on L6's line. Extension and leader lines strike through labels: P1 through 'R 1.37', E1 through 'R1 12.01' in detail-308_win.jpg. These only add cost and are never rejected (core.js:613-617).
evidence.security: All list and detail DOM is built with createElement and textContent (app.js:11-25). The one innerHTML is the generated SVG (app.js:134). In it, all text and the aria-label pass through esc() (drawing.js:15-21, 73-87), numbers go through toFixed, and the pattern id is sanitised (drawing.js:63). There is no eval or Function. There are no fetches and no external assets: index.html loads only local CSS and JS, and browser.check.js:155-158 asserts there are no non-file requests. The capacity source links are user-clicked anchors with rel=noopener.
evidence.code_quality: There is a clear split: data.js, core.js (pure logic, UMD so Node tests can load it), drawing.js (SVG serialisation) and app.js (DOM and routing). Names are readable and missing values are handled with notes rather than invented numbers. computeGeometry is a single ~290-line function (core.js:235-526), and the label placer is nested closures (core.js:584-774). This is dense but readable. Small leftovers: the unused geom parameter in titleBlock (app.js:111), and placed.arrows is collected but never read (core.js:632).
evidence.tests: core.test.js covers many of the brief's drawing rules with exact formulas. These include rim types (rebated as a synthetic case), the primer-pocket table, chamfer, rimfire half-round, groove points, belt ramp and w, and fillets. On the bullet side they cover seating and k for pointy, rounded-pistol, flat-pistol and semi-wadcutter bullets, points on the ogive arc and on the ellipse, heeled diameters, wall thicknesses, tolerance merging, angle formats, the missing-value note, and label-label and label-outline non-overlap for all 25 records. browser.check.js drives Chromium from file://. It checks search, filter, reload, the back link, a 390 px phone, dark mode, a one-page A4 PDF, the Print button, no network and no console errors. Gaps: no test catches collinear dimension lines or leaders through labels. Rounded/flat rifle factors and the α dimension form are not tested. The browser check is a plain script, not a test-runner suite.
evidence.ux_design: The drawing is legible at true scale with a dash-dot centre line, a hatched section and a seated bullet. The tables are dense, right-aligned and use tabular numbers, and the title block is clear (detail-308_win.jpg). However, the SVG is capped at max-width 560px (style.css:143) inside a 1080px panel. On desktop it fills under half the width and leaves large empty margins. Labels are struck through by other dimensions' extension lines ('R 1.37', 'R1 12.01', 'P2 11.53 -0.2' in the print). The L2/L6 dimensions on 9,3 x 74 R are ambiguous. The print layout is good: a two-column fact grid, a full-width drawing, four-column tables and a footer on one page (print-308_win.jpg). Dark mode exists in CSS (style.css:14-25) but is not shown in the screenshots.
evidence.accessibility: The SVG has role=img and aria-label '<name> drawing' (drawing.js:73-74). Search and Family have real <label for> associations. The count is aria-live. Tables use thead with scope=col and tbody th with scope=row (app.js:90-108). Facts use a dl, the toolbar is a nav, and there are focus-visible outlines (style.css:40-43). Muted text #5d636b on #fbfbf9 has adequate contrast. Weaknesses: the drawing's text alternative is just its name, with no summary of the dimensions. The tables have no caption or aria-labelledby tie to their h3.
evidence.simplicity: Plain HTML, CSS and JS with no runtime dependencies and only playwright as a dev dependency (package.json). About 1,100 lines of non-data code. The candidate-based label placer is the most complex part, and the overlap requirement justifies it. No needless abstraction.
evidence.maintainability: Present: package.json with 'test' and 'test:browser' scripts, a package-lock, unit tests and a browser check, and header comments explaining units and coordinates (core.js:1-5). Missing: there is no README, no docs, no ADRs or specs, and no CI configuration. The Node version is not pinned (no engines or .nvmrc). Playwright uses a caret range. There is no release or versioning note beyond 1.0.0. Some setup is undocumented: browser.check.js needs the Chromium binary or the CHROMIUM_PATH variable and writes to /tmp. A newcomer must reverse-engineer how to run and verify the app.
evidence.visual_design: Calm, restrained technical look: system sans-serif, one accent blue, thin rules, consistent spacing and alignment across list and detail views (list.jpg, detail-*.jpg). The drawing uses consistent stroke weights and arrowheads. Struck-through labels and the small drawing inside an oversized bordered panel make the drawing look less finished than the tables.
evidence.layout: The hierarchy follows the brief: name, facts, drawing, title block, then grouped tables in a three-column grid. The list is a clean three-column table with right-aligned L3. There is no overflow or clipping in any screenshot. The drawing panel wastes about half its width (detail-308_win.jpg, detail-300_win_mag.jpg). The facts block pushes the drawing below the first fold on short screens. Uneven table heights leave gaps in the grid (detail-9_mm_luger.jpg, Projectile alone in a row).
evidence.usability: Finding a cartridge is quick: live search across alternative names, a family filter, a count, and one click to the detail view. Routes are bookmarkable and an unknown key shows a not-found page with a way back (app.js:184-189). Print works in one click and gives a one-page sheet. Missing values are explained under the drawing ('Drawing notes: E and E1 missing; no extractor groove drawn.'). There is no way to move between cartridges from the detail view except via the list, which is acceptable.
evidence.reception: Reloaders and engineers would trust the data: values exactly as published, correct tolerances and angles, a true-to-scale outline that matches the OpenBallistics references, and a clean one-page print. A careful engineer would notice dimension lines crossing labels and the ambiguous L2/L6 on 9,3 x 74 R. They would also note that α has no angular dimension, which undermines a drawing presented as precise. The tool is likely to be reused, but they would not yet call it publication-grade.

unmet_requirements: Shoulder angle α has no angular dimension with arrowheads and extension lines; it gets a leader and label only (core.js:675-685, 735-740)

Labels not fully clear: extension and leader lines strike through labels (R, R1, P2 in detail-308_win.jpg and print-308_win.jpg); L2 and L6 dimension lines are collinear on 9,3 x 74 R (detail-9_3_x_74_r.jpg)
Title block gives no actual scale, only 'True to scale (1 mm = 1 unit); fitted to width' (app.js:123)
Straight cases: the inner wall blends tb→tn over the whole body instead of keeping tb along the body (core.js:395-397)
No README, docs, specs or ADRs from the brief's required process are in the delivery
strengths: Faithful implementation of the geometry rules (chamfer, rimfire half-round, groove, belt ramp at δ, filleted shoulder, ogive/ellipse/cone noses, heeled bullet, walls and primer pocket), true to scale and matching the reference outlines
Correct data presentation: values as published, tolerances merged, angle formats, full grouped Symbol/Value/Unit tables, and a clean one-page black-on-white A4 print
No-dependency, file://-safe vanilla JS with escaped SVG generation, plus meaningful unit tests on the rules and a Chromium browser check (search, reload, phone, dark mode, one-page print, no network)
issues: Dimension legibility defects: extension and leader lines run through other labels, and collinear dimension lines (L2/L6 on 9,3 x 74 R) make dimensions ambiguous; the placer only penalises crossings and ignores collinear overlap (core.js:537-543, 613-617)
No angular dimension for α and no real scale in the title block, so two drawing requirements are only partly met
No README, CI, docs or decision records, and the Node version is not pinned; the drawing is also capped at 560px and fills under half the desktop panel
review.verdict: The app is a solid, dependency-free reference with accurate data and drawing geometry that follows the brief's rules closely and prints cleanly on one A4 page. Labels struck through by dimension lines, ambiguous collinear dimensions, the missing α angle dimension and the missing documentation need fixing before it is published to a technical audience.
